Beállítom Az amerikai szenátus pénteken megszavazta azt az Oroszország elleni szankciós csomagot, ami lehetővé tenné, hogy az orosz kőolajat és földgázt vásárló országokra akár százszázalékos vámot vessenek ki. Az MTI arról írt, hogy a jogszabályt még 2025-ben kezdeményezte a nemrég meghalt Lindsey Graham , aki elkötelezett támogatója volt Ukrajnának. A Graham nevét viselő törvényt kétpárti támogatással fogadta el a szenátus, vagyis az amerikai parlament, a Kongresszus felsőháza. A végszavazás várhatóan szeptember elején lesz, ekkor kerül majd a törvény a képviselőház elé. A törvény másodlagos vámokról szóló része főleg az orosz energiahordozók legnagyobb vásárlóit, vagyis Indiát és Kínát érinti, de az európai vásárlókra, így Magyarországra is hatással lehet. Igaz, a törvény alól Donald Trump személyesen felmentést adhat, és a jogszabályban meghatározott intézkedések hatálya azonnal megszűnik, ha békét vagy tűzszünetet köt egymással Oroszország és Ukrajna. Éjszaka orosz rakéta- és dróntámadás ért 12 ukrajnai régiót, 13 ember meghalt, 77-en pedig megsebesültek – mondta Volodimir Zelenszkij a belgrádi sajtótájékoztatóján. Arról beszélt, hogy országszerte késtek a vonatok, mert az orosz hadsereg energetikai létesítményeket és a vasúti infrastruktúrát is támadta. Timur Tkacsenko, Kijev katonai közigazgatásának vezetője azt mondta, az ukrán főváros közelében az orosz támadásokban éjszaka legalább hárman meghaltak , köztük egy gyerek – írta a BBC. Az ukrán hadsereg orosz olajfinomítókra, az iljszkijire és a szizranyira mért csapásokat, de egy fekete-tengeri fúrótornyon lévő orosz megfigyelőállomást is támadás ért – közölte szombaton az ukrán vezérkar az MTI szerint. https://www.theguardian.com/australia-ne.text: Pauline Hanson says she is opposed to a major gun buyback being announced by Anthony Albanese and the NSW premier, Chris Minns, in Sydney shortly. Legislation for the plan passed parliament earlier this year, part of the response to the Bondi beach terror attack. It will be run in two phases, with the cost split 50:50 between the federal and NSW governments. Under the first phase of the scheme, $1,000 will be paid for revolvers and $850 for semi-automatic handguns. Compensation of $850 will be paid for double-barrel shotguns and $650 for those with a single barrel. Between $650 and $1,000 will be paid for rifles, while air rifles have a fixed compensation of $450. Hanson told News24 taxpayers should not pay for the scheme. She suggested the buyback would impact “law-abiding Australians who are trying to go about their business, like farmers that need their guns,” she said. https://www.worcesternews.co.uk/news/265.text: River Severn West Mercia Police Crime Emergency Worcestershire Worcester Men fishing in River Severn made 'threatening gestures' at pensioner By Mary Stenson Reporter Share 0 Comments 3 Skip to next photo 1 / 1 Show caption 1 / 1 Share 0 Comments This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A PENSIONER said he was "disgusted" after a group of men fishing in the river made threatening gestures at him. Paul Smith said he was walking near the River Severn in Worcester on Thursday afternoon (September 3) when he noticed the group of men on a boat fishing in the swan sanctuary area. He said he called out to the group to inform them that fishing is prohibited in this area, a rule that is made clear by signs on railings in the area. READ NEXT: Polish community's heartbreak and deep shock after Worcester murder 'They weren't joking' The 69-year-old said the men became threatening, making throat-slicing and punching gestures. He said they also started threatening to beat him up when they got off the boat. "They weren’t joking," Mr Smith said. "I was disgusted because they didn’t seem to give a damn about the rules about the swans. "I was apprehensive because I didn’t know if they were carrying knives or anything." BAN: Fishing is prohibited in the swan sanctuary area of the River Severn (Image: Supplied) As directed by the 'no fishing' sign, he called police on 101, and said he also reported the men's threatening behaviour. Mr Smith said he also made the call handler aware that he was being threatened. READ NEXT: Worcester optician keeps door locked while shop is open after thefts elsewhere Disappointed by police response He made the call at 1.03pm and was on the phone for several minutes. After 45 minutes, he left the area when police still hadn't arrived. West Mercia Police has confirmed that officers attended the scene at 2.07pm. "I waited 45 minutes for police," Mr Smith said. "They never turned up. I even tried to flag a police car down." INCIDENT: Paul Smith said he was 'disgusted' by the men's actions and 'disappointed' in the police response (Image: NQ) The force said the call was deemed 'Grade 2', meaning officers should attend within two hours. When they did arrive, officers spoke to "potential witnesses" but no suspects have been found. "Officers received reports of anti-social behaviour and illegal fishing on the River Severn yesterday, shortly after 1pm yesterday," a West Mercia Police spokesperson said. "All incidents reported to us are assessed according to the level of risk and harm they present to the public, this ensures our resources are directed the quickest to those who need them the most. "This incident was assessed as a Grade 2 response, requiring attendance within two hours. "Officers arrived at the location within one hour of the report being received, carried out a search and spoke to a number of potential witnesses. "No arrests have been made in connection to the matter. "Anyone who wishes to report anti-social behaviour is advised to contact their local safer neighbourhood team."
